payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_session.py::test_a_review_that_fits_its_pool_runs_every_session_capped_at_what_is_left stayed green with the spec's wrong version "A criterion probe that failed costs the pool nothing, so the next session's cap is $1.25 too high." applied to saffron/phases/review.py as an edit. The claim was "A REVIEW that fits REVIEW's pool runs every lens, criterion probe and wrong-version session, and reaches `READY_FOR_REVIEW` as it does today. Each session, and each re-prompt turn, is capped at what the pool has left. The pool opens at the task's remainder when REVIEW starts, floored at `REVIEW_FLOOR_USD` once per name in `review.LENSES`. Each session's reported cost comes off the pool when it ends. That cost includes the re-prompt turn of a lens, a criterion probe and a wrong-version session, and the cost of a criterion probe or wrong-version session that failed. The witness drives a remainder above that floor and two below it, with the four declared lenses and with three. The three-lens REVIEW's last session starts with exactly `REVIEW_FLOOR_USD` left.", and the whole `tests` gate stayed green under the edit too.
